open_issues: FollowUpService.RunDueRemindersAsync is implemented and idempotent (it uses ReminderScheduler.Key/KeyPrefix and ReminderScheduler.Lookback so it behaves exactly like the other reminders) but NOTHING calls it on the minute tick: ReminderScheduler.cs is outside my allowed paths and is currently modified by another agent. One line is needed in ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync (or in the shell's background pass) to call it; until then a follow-up reminder is stored but never rings.

«حذف المسودة غير المرقّمة نهائيًا» (AGREEMENT item 19) is implemented as a SOFT delete, not a physical DELETE. DATA-MODEL §0 forbids physically deleting a synced row, and correspondence has only AFTER INSERT/UPDATE change_log triggers — a physical DELETE would never reach the other devices and the draft would reappear on the next sync. The soft delete is what the user experiences as permanent (the global query filter hides it from every screen and service, and no command restores it), and the UPDATE syncs correctly. If the owner wants a true physical delete, the schema needs an AFTER DELETE trigger and a sync rule for it.

0001_initial.sql's ux_correspondence_official_number was UNIQUE on official_number ALONE, which contradicts ARCHITECTURE §5's two independent in/out sequences: registering an incoming letter and approving an outgoing one on the same day raised 'UNIQUE constraint failed' inside the transaction that had just issued the number. Fixed by 0003_correspondence_number_index.sql (drop + recreate as UNIQUE(direction, official_number), still unfiltered on deleted_at) rather than by editing 0001, which is not in my allowed paths and may already be applied on real installations. tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests/SchemaTests.cs line ~236 was updated to the new index name — worth a second opinion from whoever owns the schema.

TemplateService / LetterComposer / DerivedDocumentBuilder implementation are the next package. The readiness row «القالب مختار» only checks that correspondence.template_id is set; it does not validate the template file. IDerivedDocumentBuilder (BuildAsync + PreviewAsync) is defined in ReferralService.cs and is resolved optionally from DI — register the letter package's implementation as IDerivedDocumentBuilder and referrals start producing print copies with no change here.

ExchangeService never touches the vault: attachments are passed in as ExchangeAttachment(name, mime, bytes) on export and handed back as bytes in ExchangeImportResult.Attachments on import. B3-2 must read them from / write them to the vault and call ICorrespondenceService.LinkDocumentAsync. Likewise DeviceIdentity and DeviceCertificate are supplied by the caller, never stored by Core (no key material enters the database or a log).
The «للمستلم فقط» flag is stored and returned but the sync export filter that acts on it (ARCHITECTURE §6) belongs to the sync package; nothing here enforces it.

No NuGet package was added. Wakeel.Core gained a ProjectReference to Wakeel.Crypto (needed for the .wakeel-msg containers). Wakeel.Crypto references no project, so this adds no cycle, and Wakeel.UI already had both references. Note that Wakeel.Crypto's types (including its own DeviceKind enum) are now transitively visible to every project that references Core.
notes:
PUBLIC API THE SCREEN PACKAGES CONSUME (namespace Wakeel.Core.Services.Correspondence, all Scoped in AddWakeelCore):

ICorrespondenceService — Validate(input, today) -> IReadOnlyList<CorrespondenceValidationIssue>; CreateDraftAsync / UpdateDraftAsync (the 3-second autosave of item 32; refused once numbered); GetAsync / ListAsync(CorrespondenceQuery); ScanForDuplicatesAsync (while typing, writes nothing); RegisterIncomingAsync -> IncomingRegistrationResult(View, OfficialNumber, NearLimitWarning, Suspected); GetReadinessAsync -> ReadinessChecklist(Items, SummaryAr, IsReady, CurrentStep); ApproveOutgoingAsync -> ApprovalResult; DeleteDraftAsync; CancelAsync(reason); CloseAsync(note); ArchiveAsync; ChangeStatusAsync; SetRecipientOnlyAsync; SetLinksAsync(CorrespondenceLinks); LinkDocumentAsync.
IDuplicateDetector — ScanAsync, RecordSuspectedAsync, GetReviewsAsync, MarkNotDuplicateAsync («ليست مكررة»), MarkDuplicateAsync; statics DuplicateDetector.SubjectSimilarity / Words / Jaccard and the constant SubjectThreshold = 0.8.
IReferralService — CreateAsync, PreviewAsync (the «ستُضاف صفحة» warning before saving, item 34), ListAsync, MarkAnsweredAsync, CloseAsync.
IFollowUpService — AddAsync(kind, note, now, nextAt, reminderAt, statusTo), ListAsync, GetAwaitingReplyCardAsync, ListAwaitingReplyAsync, RunDueRemindersAsync.
ICorrectionService — ApplyAsync(changes, reason, now), ListAsync; CorrectionService.CorrectableFields is the whitelist a W25 form should render.
IExchangeService — ExportAsync(ExchangeExportRequest), PreviewImportAsync, ImportAsync, ListLogAsync.
CorrespondenceStateMachine.AllowedFrom / CanTransition — use it to grey out commands a state does not offer.
CorrespondenceRefusedException carries MessageAr (a finished Arabic sentence) and, for field checks, Issues; show MessageAr directly, do NOT send it through IErrorMapper.

DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING
1. Namespace vs entity: the namespace «…Services.Correspondence» shadows the entity type «Correspondence», so every file in the folder aliases it as CorrespondenceRow. Screen packages that import both need the same alias.
2. Every view model is already Arabic: CorrespondenceView carries StatusAr/DirectionAr/ConfidentialityAr/RecipientOnlyAr/DueAr/UpdatedAr/CurrentStepAr; ReferralView, FollowupView, AwaitingReplyCard, DuplicateReviewView and ExchangeLogView the same. Screens must never map an enum to a word of their own. All new strings live in CoreAr (CorrStatus*, CorrStep*, CorrReady*, CorrValidation*, CorrRefused*, CorrDuplicate*, CorrFollowup*, CorrReferral*, CorrExchange*, CorrAudit*).
3. Numbering: both RegisterIncomingAsync and ApproveOutgoingAsync run the ARCHITECTURE §9 clock check themselves (a bad clock becomes the Arabic «لن تُصدر أرقام رسمية حتى التصحيح», not the numbering service's English contract message), then open ONE transaction, issue the number, write the row and the audit entry, and commit. On any failure the transaction is rolled back AND every tracked entry is reloaded/detached, so the official_numbers sequence does not silently skip a number — asserted by a test that makes the duplicate detector throw right after numbering and then proves the next registration still gets 001.
4. Readiness checklist (item 18): 5 rows — subject, recipient, template, document (body text OR a linked Original), and «لم تُعتمد بعد» (the double-click guard of item 32). The checklist refusal is raised BEFORE the field checks, because the review screen is where the user is standing. GetReadinessAsync/GetAsync compute it; ListAsync deliberately does not (it would be one extra read per row), so CorrespondenceView.CurrentStep is null in list results.
5. Freezing: once numbered, UpdateDraftAsync and a second approval are refused, and LinkDocumentAsync accepts only Attachment (Original/DerivedPrint are frozen). Changes then go through ICorrectionService, which refuses an unnumbered item, refuses a field outside CorrectableFields (the number, the issue date, the approval stamp and the direction are never correctable), refuses an empty reason and refuses a no-op, and stores {field, old, new} JSON so both versions survive.
6. Transitions: Draft -> New only (through registration/approval); the three working states move freely; Done/Closed can be reopened into InProgress; Cancelled -> Archived only; Archived is terminal; a same-to-same move is refused. Every transition writes an audit_log row AND a followups row of kind Status carrying status_from/status_to, so the timeline and the audit never disagree. FollowUpService.AddAsync(statusTo:) does the move on the SAME entry, so one office action is one timeline row.
7. ReferralStatus.Overdue is derived on read, never stored — no background pass is needed to keep it true.
8. Duplicates: exact = same external_number AND same party/unit -> refused before the transaction opens; suspected = same number with another party, or normalised-subject Jaccard >= 0.8 -> registered and written as pending duplicate_reviews rows. Cancelled items are excluded from the comparison (a withdrawn letter must not block re-registering the real one); drafts are included. The subject comparison looks back over DuplicateDetector.SubjectScanLimit = 2000 items of the same direction, newest first; the number checks are indexed and see everything. Subject words come from ArabicText.Normalize plus a punctuation split, so tashkeel, tatweel, ة/ه and ى/ي never decide a match — tested on real Arabic subjects.
9. Exchange: the package is opened TWICE — once with VerifyCertificateChain=false only to read the producer's organisation id (its signature over the manifest is checked either way), then, when that organisation is ours, again WITH the chain checked against the pinned org key. Same org => internal incoming (item 49, the unit is resolved from the structure by unit id then by office code); different org => external incoming (item 22). Every container refusal becomes one plain sentence, «التوقيع غير سليم؛ لا تسجّل هذا الملف». The sender's own official number becomes the recipient's external_number. Re-importing the same package is recognised in the preview and refused on import, so one letter never consumes two incoming numbers. The org's recovery copy of the content key rides in the manifest (item 17).
10. Measurements: 8 source files (~2,900 lines) + 2 index migrations; 8 test files, 112 new tests; the suite runs 449 tests in ~22 s; build is 0 warnings with TreatWarningsAsErrors.
